# `gridmetrics`: the full metric grid {#sec-gridmetrics}

## What it does

`gridmetrics` is the workhorse of area-based forest inventory. For every
grid cell, it computes a large set of statistics from the heights and
intensities of the returns in that cell: height percentiles, mean and
variability, canopy cover, return counts, per-layer summaries, and
surface roughness. Models fit between these cell metrics and field plot
measurements (volume, biomass, basal area) are then applied to every cell
to map those attributes across a whole project area.

`gridmetrics` runs on one file, as here, or on a whole folder of tiles in
a batch mode that tiles, buffers, and processes them in parallel
(@sec-many-tiles). @sec-metrics defines every metric.

## Options used

| Option | Value | What it does |
|:--------|:--------------------|:-------------------------|
| (second input) | `out/ground_dem.tif` | Ground surface, given as the second positional argument. `/ground:` works too. |
| `/cellsize` | `10` | Cell size, 10 ft. Match it to the size of your field plots when the grid will be used for plot-based models. |
| `/outdir` | `out/gridmetrics` | Folder for the raster, named `<input name>_gridmetrics.tif`. |
| `/strata` | `0.5,2,5,10,20` | Also summarize the returns in each of six height layers (@sec-densitymetrics). |
| `/strataraster` | | Write the per-layer summaries as raster bands, not only as table columns. |
| `/surfstats` | | Add `surface_area_ratio` and `roughness` bands computed from the highest return in each cell (@sec-gridsurfacestats). |
| `/output-table` | `out/gridmetrics/gridmetrics_table.csv` | Also write every metric as a CSV table, one row per cell. |
| `/profile` | | Print high-resolution execution timing breakdown (data read & decompression, spatial binning & ground interpolation, metric computation, and raster serialization) to stderr. |

: Options used in the `gridmetrics` example. {#tbl-options-gridmetrics}

Options left at their defaults include `/minht:2` (returns below 2 ft
are left out of the height statistics), `/nodata:NA`, and `/noheight:0`
(@sec-conventions).

## Native Raster DSM Ingestion

In addition to point cloud files (`.las`, `.laz`), `gridmetrics` natively ingests high-resolution Digital Surface Model (DSM) rasters (`.tif`, `.tiff`, `.vrt`, `.img`):

- **Scanline Streaming**: Rasters are processed in 512-row scanline chunks using `GDALRaster::ReadBandWindow`, bounding host memory consumption under 250 MB regardless of raster tile size.
- **Bilinear Ground Subtraction**: Ground elevations from the DTM are evaluated at continuous fine-pixel centers via bilinear interpolation, ensuring sub-pixel vertical accuracy.
- **Metric Parity**: Normalized pixel heights feed into standard `CellAccumulator` bins and `ComputePointStatBundle`, producing identical multi-band GeoTIFF metric rasters and CSV tables.

## Outputs

- **`TC_1372_forest200ft_gridmetrics.tif`**: one multiband GeoTIFF with
  176 named bands on this run. They include height statistics
  (`elev_min` to `elev_p99`, L-moments, and others), canopy cover and
  its variants (`canopy_cover`, `allcover`, `afcover`, and others),
  `point_density`, counts by return number (`r1count` to `r9count`),
  intensity statistics (`int_*`), `surface_area_ratio`, `roughness`, and
  seven bands per height layer (density, count, proportion, mean,
  standard deviation, minimum, maximum), plus six intensity bands per
  layer.
- **`gridmetrics_table.csv`**: one row per cell. It starts with the
  cell's column, row, and center coordinates (`Col`, `Row`, `X`, `Y`),
  its `TotalReturns` and `FirstReturns`, and `CanopyCover` and
  `PointDensity`, followed by the raster's metrics with the same names.
  The surface-roughness bands and the per-layer density bands are in the
  raster only.

`/output-mode:singleband` writes each metric as its own GeoTIFF instead.

## Results

@fig-gridmetrics-maps shows six representative bands, each on its own
scale. Maximum and 95th-percentile height follow the same crown pattern
as the canopy height model (@fig-canopymodel-maps) at a coarser cell
size. Canopy cover is high across this closed-canopy tile. Height
variability is highest where tall crowns sit next to gaps.

{{< include ../examples/fragments/gridmetrics_figures.md >}}

## Checks

@tbl-checks-gridmetrics confirms that the grid has the expected rows and
columns and sits on the tile, that no band is empty everywhere, that the
per-cell return counts match R, that no maximum height exceeds the
tallest point, and that the table has one row per cell and agrees with
the raster.

{{< include ../examples/fragments/gridmetrics_checks.md >}}
